question: Simplify: frac{(tan² beta operatorname{cosec}² beta)}{(1+tan² beta)}
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Substitute an angle, say β = 30°, into the expression to quickly evaluate it.

Numerator = tan² 30° × cosec² 30° = (1/√3)² × 2² = 1/3 × 4 = 4/3

Denominator = 1 + tan² 30° = 1 + (1/√3)² = 1 + 1/3 = 4/3

Expression = (4/3) ÷ (4/3) = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

(tan² β × cosec² β) ÷ (1 + tan² β)

**Formula Used:**

1 + tan² θ = sec² θ

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ

cosec θ = 1 / sin θ

sec θ = 1 / cos θ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Numerator = tan² β × cosec² β

⇒ Numerator = (sin² β / cos² β) × (1 / sin² β)

⇒ Numerator = 1 / cos² β = sec² β

⇒ Denominator = 1 + tan² β

⇒ Denominator = sec² β

⇒ Expression = Numerator ÷ Denominator

⇒ Expression = sec² β / sec² β = 1

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 | sec² θ − tan² θ = 1 | cosec² θ − cot² θ = 1

Reciprocal Identities

sin θ = 1 / cosec θ | cos θ = 1 / sec θ | tan θ = 1 / cot θ

Quotient Identities

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ | cot θ = cos θ / sin θ
